caption: A flashlight is pointed at a mirror on the wall, and a spot of light appears on the opposite wall.

sa.check: A mirror hangs on a wall.
A flashlight is pointed at it.
A spot of light appears on the opposite wall.
The flashlight is aimed first and the spot appears with it.

pc.expect: The spot appears when the beam hits the mirror and vanishes when the beam leaves it.
pc.fail: The spot is there with the beam off the mirror; or the beam hits the mirror and no spot appears; or the spot remains after the beam has left.

pc.expect: The spot moves the opposite way when the flashlight is angled, as a reflected beam does.
pc.fail: It moves the same way as the flashlight; or stays still while the flashlight turns; or jumps.

pc.expect: The spot does not move on its own.
pc.fail: It slides with the flashlight still; or flickers with the beam steady.

pc.expect: The spot is one bright patch with a soft edge.
pc.fail: It splits into several under one beam; or it is a sharp geometric shape; or it floods the room.

pc.expect: One flashlight, one mirror and one spot.
pc.fail: A second spot appears; or the mirror duplicates; or the spot becomes solid; or the beam passes through the wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The walls and the mirror frame stay the same.
pc.fail: A wall changes colour; or the frame changes; or the room rearranges.
